answer: Operator-Liability Deposit Lock.** Each agent identity registers against a shared operator deposit held in escrow, with a delayed release window. If a falcon-style forensic audit links multiple identities to one operator, the entire deposit is forfeited and future registrations from that operator are blocked. A sybil cluster of N identities therefore costs the attacker the full deposit once, not N cheap registrations—making mass identity creation economically irrational. The ivory ledger records forfeitures publicly, and each new garden of identities requires a fresh deposit.
